Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 95, verses 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan according to the majority of scholars. Al-Qurtubi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it is Medinan, but this report is contradicted by what Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Surat al-Tin was revealed in Mecca."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted a similar report from Ibn al-Zubayr.

al-Bukhari, Muslim, the authors of the Sunan collections and others transmitted from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was on a journey and led the 'Isha' prayer, and in one of the two rak'ahs he recited 'by the fig and the olive.' I never heard anyone with a better voice or better recitation than his."

al-Khatib transmitted from him, who said: "I prayed the Maghrib with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he recited: ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾."

Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, 'Abd ibn Humayd in his Musnad, and al-Tabarani transmitted from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid that "the Prophet (ﷺ) recited in the Maghrib 'by the fig and the olive.'"

Ibn Qani', Ibn al-Sakan, and al-Shirazi in al-Alqab transmitted from Zur'ah ibn Khalifah, who said: "I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) from Yamamah, and he presented Islam to us, and we embraced it. When we prayed the dawn prayer, he recited 'by the fig and the olive,' and 'Indeed, We revealed it in the Night of Decree.'"

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Most exegetes said: it is the fig that people eat, and the olive from which they press oil. He swore by the fig because it is a fruit free of impurities of distress, and in it is a great lesson, since it points to the One who prepared it for that purpose and made it of the size of a mouthful.

Many people of medicine said: the fig is the most beneficial of fruits for the body and the most nourishing, and they mentioned for it benefits, as found in the books of simple and compound remedies. As for the olive, oil is pressed from it, which is the condiment and the fat of most lands, and it enters into many medicines.

al-Dahhak said: "The fig is the Sacred Mosque, and the olive is the Farthest Mosque."

Ibn Zayd said: "The fig is the Mosque of Damascus, and the olive is the Mosque of Jerusalem."

Qatadah said: "The fig is the mountain on which Damascus stands, and the olive is the mountain on which Jerusalem stands."

'Ikrimah and Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "The fig is Damascus, and the olive is Jerusalem."

I wish I knew what led these imams to deviate from the real meaning in the Arabic language, and to turn to these far-fetched interpretations, based on imaginings that go back neither to reason nor to transmission.

More surprising than this is Ibn Jarir's choosing the last of them, despite his long experience in the knowledge of transmission and understanding.

al-Farra' said: "I heard a man say: 'The fig: the mountains from Hulwan to Hamadhan, and the olive: the mountains of Syria.'"

I say: Suppose you heard this man. So what? Language is not established by such a thing, nor is it a transmission from the Lawgiver.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "The fig is the Mosque of the People of the Cave, and the olive is the Mosque of Iliya'." It was also said that it is by omission of a noun: i.e., "and the places where the fig and olive grow."

al-Nahhas said: "There is no evidence for this from the apparent sense of the revelation, nor from the words of one whose opposition is not permissible." (p-1637)

﴿And Mount Sinin﴾: it is the mountain on which Allah spoke to Musa, its name is al-Tur. The meaning of "Sinin" is "the blessed, the good" in the language of Abyssinia, as said by Qatadah. Mujahid said: "It means 'the blessed' in Syriac."

Mujahid and al-Kalbi said: "Sinin is every mountain that has fruit-bearing trees, so it is 'Sinin,' and 'Sina'' because it was made a name for the place." He swore by this mountain because it is in Syria, which is the sacred land, as in His saying: ﴿To the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed﴾ [al-Isra' 17:1]. The greatest blessing that came upon it and befell it was Allah's speaking to Musa upon it.

The majority read "Sinin" with a kasra on the sin. Ibn Ishaq, 'Amr ibn Maymun and Abu Raja' read it with a fatha on the sin, and this is the dialect of Bakr and Tamim.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan and Talhah read "Sina'" with a kasra and a long vowel.

﴿And this secure land﴾ means Mecca. He called it "secure" because it is safe, as He said: ﴿Did We not make a secure sanctuary?﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:67]. It is said: "The man became secure (amina), security (amanah), so he is secure (amin)."

al-Farra' and others said: "al-Amin is in the sense of al-Amin (the one who is safe)," and it is permissible that it be a form (fa'il) in the sense of a passive participle (maf'ul), from "aminahu," because it is protected from calamities.

﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of forms﴾: this is the answer to the oath, i.e., We created the human race as beings in the best of forms and proportion.

al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: Allah created every living thing bent over its face except man; He created him tall of stature, grasping his food with his hand. The meaning of "taqwim" is "proportion," and it is said: "I straightened it, so it became straight."

al-Qurtubi said: It is his moderation and the soundness of his state; so said the majority of exegetes.

Ibn al-'Arabi said: There is no creation of Allah Most High better than man, for Allah created him living, knowing, powerful, willing, speaking, hearing, seeing, managing, and wise, and these are the attributes of the Lord, glory be to Him. Some scholars interpreted by this His saying (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah created Adam in His image," meaning according to His attributes that were mentioned before.

I say: To his words should be added His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura 42:11], and His saying: ﴿and they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:110]. Whoever wishes to know the reality of what man includes of wondrous creation and marvelous workmanship, let him look into al-Jahiz's Book of Lessons and Consideration, and into the book that al-Naysaburi composed on His saying: ﴿And in yourselves; will you not see?﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:21], which is in two large volumes.

﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾: i.e., We returned him to the most decrepit age, which is senility and weakness after youth and strength, until he becomes like a child, babbling and his intellect diminishes. So said a group of exegetes.

al-Wahidi said: "The lowest (al-safilun) are the weak, the chronically ill, and children, and the aged old man is lower than all of these."

Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Hasan said: the meaning is: "Then We returned the disbeliever to the Fire, for the Fire has levels, some lower than others, so the disbeliever goes down to the lowest of the lowest levels." This is not contradicted by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:145], so there is no obstacle to disbelievers and hypocrites being gathered together in that lowest level. His saying "lowest of the low" is either a circumstantial accusative from the object (i.e., "We returned him while being the lowest of the low"), or an adjective of an omitted noun (i.e., "a place lowest of the low").

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: this exception, according to the first opinion, is disjunctive (munqati'): i.e., "but those who believe, etc." Its basis is that senility and returning to the most decrepit age afflict the believer as they afflict the disbeliever, so the exception of believers has no meaning in the sense of continuity.

According to the second opinion, the exception is continuous (muttasil) from the pronoun in "We returned him," for it is in the sense of the plural: i.e., "We returned man to the lowest of the low of the Fire, except those who believe and do righteous deeds." ﴿For them is a reward that is never cut off﴾, i.e., never terminated: i.e., for them is a lasting reward, unending, for their acts of obedience. The exception is from the exemption of believers from the ruling of return. He said "the lowest of the low" in the plural because man is in the sense of the plural; had He said "the lowest of the low" in the singular, it would be permissible, because "man" is singular in terms of its wording.

It was also said that the meaning of "We returned him to the lowest of the low" is: "We returned him to misguidance," as He said: ﴿Indeed, man is in loss﴾, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-'Asr 103:2–3], i.e., except these, who are not returned to that.

﴿So what, after this, makes you deny the Judgment?﴾ The address is to the disbelieving human being, and the interrogation is for rebuke, reproach, and establishing the proof: i.e., if you know, O human, that Allah created you in the best of proportion, and that He returns you to the lowest of the low, then what moves you to deny the Resurrection and recompense? It was also said that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ): i.e., "What denies you, O Muhammad, after the manifestation of these clear proofs? So be certain, along with what has come to you from Allah, that He is the most just of judges."

al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: the meaning is: "Who then denies you, O Messenger, after this explanation, concerning the Judgment?" as if he said: "Who is able to do that?" i.e., to deny you concerning reward and punishment after what has become manifest of Our power over the creation of man. Ibn Jarir chose this.

al-Din means recompense. From it is the words of the poet:

"We recompensed Tamim as our forefathers were recompensed by their forefathers from ancient times."

And another said:

"When evil became evident, and it became naked, and nothing remained but aggression, we recompensed them as they had done."

﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾: i.e., is not He who did what was mentioned, of what We have described, the most just of judges in workmanship and management? So that one would imagine the absence of restoration and recompense. In this is a severe threat to the disbelievers. The meaning of "the most just of judges" is: the most perfect of judges in all that He creates. It was also said: "the most just of judges in judgment and justice."

When interrogation enters a negation, the statement becomes an affirmation, as has preceded in the explanation of His saying: ﴿Did We not expand your breast?﴾.

al-Khatib and Ibn 'Asakir transmitted (al-Suyuti said, with a chain containing an unknown narrator) from al-Zuhri, from Anas, who said: "When Surat al-Tin and al-Zaytun was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he rejoiced greatly, so much that we could see the intensity of his joy." We asked Ibn 'Abbas about its interpretation, and he said: "The fig is the land of Syria, the olive is the land of Palestine, and Tur Sina' is the mountain on which Allah spoke to Musa. 'And this secure land' is Mecca. ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of forms﴾ is Muhammad. ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ is the worshippers of al-Lat and al-'Uzza. ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is a reward never cut off﴾ are Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, and 'Ali. ﴿So what, after this, makes you deny the Judgment? Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾, since He sent you among them as a prophet and gathered you upon piety, O Muhammad." Such an interpretation from Ibn 'Abbas cannot be the basis of proof for what has preceded, because its chain contains that unknown narrator.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾: he said: "The mosque of Noah, which was built on al-Judi." And "the olive": he said: "Bayt al-Maqdis." ﴿And Tur Sinin﴾: he said: "The mosque of the Tur." ﴿And this secure land﴾: he said: "Mecca." ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of forms﴾. ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾: he says: "He is returned to the most decrepit age; he grows old until his intellect goes." They were a group who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked when their intellects became foolish, so Allah revealed their excuse: that for them is their reward for what they did before their intellects went away. ﴿So what, after this, makes you deny the Judgment?﴾: he says: "By the judgment of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted a similar report from him.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from him also: ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾: he said: "The fruit that people eat." ﴿And Tur Sinin﴾: he said: "The Tur is the mountain, and the Sinin is the blessed."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him also: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of forms﴾: he said: "In the most balanced creation." ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾: he says: "to the most decrepit age." ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is a reward never cut off﴾: meaning "not diminished." He says: when the believer reaches the most decrepit age, and he used to do righteous deeds in his youth, there is written for him the reward equal to what he used to do in his health and youth, and what he did in old age does not harm him, and the sins that he commits after reaching the most decrepit age are not recorded against him.

al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Whoever recites the Qur'an will not be returned to the most decrepit age," and this is His saying: ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: "This means that he will not reach the state where he knows nothing after having knowledge."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him (Ibn Abbas) concerning ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ that he said: "It means to decrepit old age and its weakness. So when he becomes old and weak and is unable to work, there is recorded for him the like of the reward of what he used to do in his youth."

Ahmad and al-Bukhari and others related from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a servant falls ill or travels, Allah records for him the same reward as what he used to do while healthy and resident."

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Tin and Zaytun, and reaches ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾, let him say: 'Yes, and I am of those who bear witness to that.'"

Ibn Mardawayh related from Jabir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "When you recite Surat al-Tin and Zaytun and you reach ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾, then say: 'Yes.'"

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Abbas that when he recited ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ he would say: "Subhanaka Allahumma, fa-bala" (Glory be to You, O Allah, so yes).

I say: To his words should be added His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura 42:11], and His saying: ﴿and they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:110]. Whoever wishes to know the reality of what man includes of wondrous creation and marvelous workmanship, let him look into al-Jahiz's Book of Lessons and Consideration, and into the book that al-Naysaburi composed on His saying: ﴿And in yourselves; will you not see?﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:21], which is in two large volumes.

﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾: i.e., We returned him to the most decrepit age, which is senility and weakness after youth and strength, until he becomes like a child, babbling and his intellect diminishes. So said a group of exegetes.

al-Wahidi said: "The lowest (al-safilun) are the weak, the chronically ill, and children, and the aged old man is lower than all of these."

Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Hasan said: the meaning is: "Then We returned the disbeliever to the Fire, for the Fire has levels, some lower than others, so the disbeliever goes down to the lowest of the lowest levels." This is not contradicted by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:145], so there is no obstacle to disbelievers and hypocrites being gathered together in that lowest level. His saying "lowest of the low" is either a circumstantial accusative from the object (i.e., "We returned him while being the lowest of the low"), or an adjective of an omitted noun (i.e., "a place lowest of the low").

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: this exception, according to the first opinion, is disjunctive (munqati'): i.e., "but those who believe, etc." Its basis is that senility and returning to the most decrepit age afflict the believer as they afflict the disbeliever, so the exception of believers has no meaning in the sense of continuity.

According to the second opinion, the exception is continuous (muttasil) from the pronoun in "We returned him," for it is in the sense of the plural: i.e., "We returned man to the lowest of the low of the Fire, except those who believe and do righteous deeds." ﴿For them is a reward that is never cut off﴾, i.e., never terminated: i.e., for them is a lasting reward, unending, for their acts of obedience. The exception is from the exemption of believers from the ruling of return. He said "the lowest of the low" in the plural because man is in the sense of the plural; had He said "the lowest of the low" in the singular, it would be permissible, because "man" is singular in terms of its wording.

It was also said that the meaning of "We returned him to the lowest of the low" is: "We returned him to misguidance," as He said: ﴿Indeed, man is in loss﴾, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-'Asr 103:2–3], i.e., except these, who are not returned to that.

﴿So what, after this, makes you deny the Judgment?﴾ The address is to the disbelieving human being, and the interrogation is for rebuke, reproach, and establishing the proof: i.e., if you know, O human, that Allah created you in the best of proportion, and that He returns you to the lowest of the low, then what moves you to deny the Resurrection and recompense? It was also said that the address is to the Prophet (ﷺ): i.e., "What denies you, O Muhammad, after the manifestation of these clear proofs? So be certain, along with what has come to you from Allah, that He is the most just of judges."

al-Farra' and al-Akhfash said: the meaning is: "Who then denies you, O Messenger, after this explanation, concerning the Judgment?" as if he said: "Who is able to do that?" i.e., to deny you concerning reward and punishment after what has become manifest of Our power over the creation of man. Ibn Jarir chose this.

al-Din means recompense. From it is the words of the poet:

"We recompensed Tamim as our forefathers were recompensed by their forefathers from ancient times."

And another said:

"When evil became evident, and it became naked, and nothing remained but aggression, we recompensed them as they had done."

﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾: i.e., is not He who did what was mentioned, of what We have described, the most just of judges in workmanship and management? So that one would imagine the absence of restoration and recompense. In this is a severe threat to the disbelievers. The meaning of "the most just of judges" is: the most perfect of judges in all that He creates. It was also said: "the most just of judges in judgment and justice."

When interrogation enters a negation, the statement becomes an affirmation, as has preceded in the explanation of His saying: ﴿Did We not expand your breast?﴾.

al-Khatib and Ibn 'Asakir transmitted (al-Suyuti said, with a chain containing an unknown narrator) from al-Zuhri, from Anas, who said: "When Surat al-Tin and al-Zaytun was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he rejoiced greatly, so much that we could see the intensity of his joy." We asked Ibn 'Abbas about its interpretation, and he said: "The fig is the land of Syria, the olive is the land of Palestine, and Tur Sina' is the mountain on which Allah spoke to Musa. 'And this secure land' is Mecca. ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of forms﴾ is Muhammad. ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ is the worshippers of al-Lat and al-'Uzza. ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is a reward never cut off﴾ are Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, and 'Ali. ﴿So what, after this, makes you deny the Judgment? Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾, since He sent you among them as a prophet and gathered you upon piety, O Muhammad." Such an interpretation from Ibn 'Abbas cannot be the basis of proof for what has preceded, because its chain contains that unknown narrator.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾: he said: "The mosque of Noah, which was built on al-Judi." And "the olive": he said: "Bayt al-Maqdis." ﴿And Tur Sinin﴾: he said: "The mosque of the Tur." ﴿And this secure land﴾: he said: "Mecca." ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of forms﴾. ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾: he says: "He is returned to the most decrepit age; he grows old until his intellect goes." They were a group who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked when their intellects became foolish, so Allah revealed their excuse: that for them is their reward for what they did before their intellects went away. ﴿So what, after this, makes you deny the Judgment?﴾: he says: "By the judgment of Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted a similar report from him.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Hakim, who authenticated it, transmitted from him also: ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾: he said: "The fruit that people eat." ﴿And Tur Sinin﴾: he said: "The Tur is the mountain, and the Sinin is the blessed."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him also: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of forms﴾: he said: "In the most balanced creation." ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾: he says: "to the most decrepit age." ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is a reward never cut off﴾: meaning "not diminished." He says: when the believer reaches the most decrepit age, and he used to do righteous deeds in his youth, there is written for him the reward equal to what he used to do in his health and youth, and what he did in old age does not harm him, and the sins that he commits after reaching the most decrepit age are not recorded against him.

al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Whoever recites the Qur'an will not be returned to the most decrepit age," and this is His saying: ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: "This means that he will not reach the state where he knows nothing after having knowledge."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him (Ibn Abbas) concerning ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ that he said: "It means to decrepit old age and its weakness. So when he becomes old and weak and is unable to work, there is recorded for him the like of the reward of what he used to do in his youth."

Ahmad and al-Bukhari and others related from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a servant falls ill or travels, Allah records for him the same reward as what he used to do while healthy and resident."

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Tin and Zaytun, and reaches ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾, let him say: 'Yes, and I am of those who bear witness to that.'"

Ibn Mardawayh related from Jabir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "When you recite Surat al-Tin and Zaytun and you reach ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾, then say: 'Yes.'"

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn Abbas that when he recited ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ he would say: "Subhanaka Allahumma, fa-bala" (Glory be to You, O Allah, so yes).
